guardrails.name: No Secrets in Code
guardrails.rule: Code must not contain hard-coded secrets, API keys, or credentials.
enforcement: pattern
guardrails.reason: Prevents credential leakage into the repository.
verification: pattern scan
secret scan

guardrails.name: No Client Database Access
guardrails.rule: Client and UI code must never reach the database directly.
enforcement: import
guardrails.reason: Enforces the entry → service → repository → database boundary.
verification: import validation

guardrails.name: Authorization Before Access
guardrails.rule: Private resource access must be preceded by authorization.
enforcement: pattern
guardrails.reason: Prevents unauthorized access to data.
verification: review

guardrails.name: No Unsafe Dynamic Code Execution
guardrails.rule: Never eval or construct functions from untrusted input.
enforcement: pattern
guardrails.reason: Dynamic execution of untrusted input enables RCE.
verification: pattern scan

guardrails.name: Parameterized Queries Only
guardrails.rule: SQL must never be assembled by string concatenation or interpolation.
enforcement: pattern
guardrails.reason: Prevents SQL injection.
verification: pattern scan
review

guardrails.name: No Empty Catch Blocks
guardrails.rule: Every catch must log, wrap, or rethrow with context.
enforcement: pattern
guardrails.reason: Swallowed errors make failures undiagnosable.
verification: pattern scan

guardrails.name: No TODO/FIXME Left in Committed Code
guardrails.rule: Committed code must not contain TODO, FIXME, or HACK markers.
enforcement: pattern
guardrails.reason: Unresolved markers indicate unfinished or fragile work.
verification: pattern scan

guardrails.name: No Console Debug Logging in Production Paths
guardrails.rule: Production code must log through the observability module, not the console.
enforcement: pattern
guardrails.reason: Console logging bypasses structured, correlation-carrying logging.
verification: pattern scan

guardrails.name: No Explicit `any` in TypeScript
guardrails.rule: Module boundaries must be fully typed.
enforcement: pattern
guardrails.reason: `any` defeats the type system and hides defects.
verification: pattern scan
typecheck

guardrails.name: Tests Required for New Logic
guardrails.rule: Scoped source files must have an adjacent test file.
enforcement: test
guardrails.reason: New logic without tests cannot be verified.
verification: adjacent test check

guardrails.name: No Business Logic in Entry/Controller Layer
guardrails.rule: Controllers must not import repository, persistence, or domain-model internals.
enforcement: file-boundary
guardrails.reason: Keeps business logic out of the HTTP layer and honors the dependency rule.
verification: boundary validation

guardrails.name: No Direct Filesystem Access from API Layer
guardrails.rule: The API/entry layer must not touch the filesystem directly.
enforcement: import
guardrails.reason: Filesystem concerns belong in dedicated infrastructure adapters.
verification: import validation

guardrails.name: No Hardcoded URLs or Connection Strings
guardrails.rule: Environment-specific endpoints and connection strings must not be literals in code.
enforcement: pattern
guardrails.reason: Environment-specific values belong in validated configuration.
verification: pattern scan

guardrails.name: Domain Layer Has No Framework Dependencies
guardrails.rule: Domain modules must not import HTTP or framework modules.
enforcement: file-boundary
guardrails.reason: Keeps business rules framework-agnostic and testable.
verification: boundary validation

guardrails.name: Auth: CSRF protection on state-changing endpoints
guardrails.rule: State-changing API endpoints (POST, PUT, DELETE) must validate CSRF tokens.
enforcement: Middleware: CSRF token validation on mutation endpoints
guardrails.reason: Without CSRF protection, attackers can trick users into performing unwanted actions.
verification: Verify CSRF middleware is applied to all state-changing endpoints

guardrails.name: Auth: Rate limit login attempts
guardrails.rule: Login and authentication endpoints must have rate limiting.
enforcement: Middleware: rate limiting on auth endpoints
guardrails.reason: Unlimited login attempts enable brute-force attacks on user credentials.
verification: Verify rate limiting is applied to auth endpoints

guardrails.name: CI/CD: No secrets in pipeline logs
guardrails.rule: CI/CD pipelines must mask or redact secrets in output logs.
enforcement: CI: use secret masking in pipeline configuration
guardrails.reason: Unmasked secrets in CI logs are exposed to anyone with repo access.
verification: Verify pipeline configuration masks secrets

guardrails.name: CI/CD: Tests must pass before deployment
guardrails.rule: Deployment steps must depend on test pipeline success.
enforcement: Pipeline: deploy jobs depend on test jobs
guardrails.reason: Deploying without passing tests ships broken code to production.
verification: Verify deploy jobs depend on test job success

guardrails.name: Data: No string concatenation in SQL queries
guardrails.rule: SQL queries must use parameterized queries, not string concatenation.
enforcement: lint rule: detect string interpolation in SQL
guardrails.reason: String concatenation in SQL enables injection attacks that can read, modify, or delete data.
verification: Verify all SQL queries use parameterized statements

guardrails.name: Environment: Never commit .env files
guardrails.rule: .env files must be in .gitignore and never committed to version control.
enforcement: CI: detect .env files in git history
guardrails.reason: Committed .env files expose credentials to anyone with repo access.
verification: Verify .env is in .gitignore and not in git history

guardrails.name: Environment: No default/placeholder secrets
guardrails.rule: Configuration files must not contain default, placeholder, or example secret values.
enforcement: CI: detect placeholder secrets in config
guardrails.reason: Default secrets are often deployed to production, creating security vulnerabilities.
verification: Verify no placeholder secrets in configuration

guardrails.name: Errors: Never expose internal errors to clients
guardrails.rule: API error responses must not contain stack traces, database errors, or internal paths.
enforcement: CI: scan error responses for sensitive data
guardrails.reason: Internal error details reveal system architecture and potential attack vectors.
verification: Verify error responses contain only safe messages

guardrails.name: Infrastructure: No unrestricted public ingress
guardrails.rule: Cloud resources must not expose ports 0.0.0.0/0 without security group restrictions.
enforcement: IaC scan: detect unrestricted CIDR rules
guardrails.reason: Unrestricted public ingress exposes all services to the internet.
verification: Verify security groups restrict ingress to known CIDRs

guardrails.name: Mobile: No sensitive data in device logs
guardrails.rule: Logs must not contain PII, tokens, or credentials in mobile release builds.
enforcement: CI: strip console.log from release builds
guardrails.reason: Mobile device logs can be accessed by other apps or extracted from devices.
verification: Verify no sensitive data in release logs

guardrails.name: Performance: External call timeout required
guardrails.rule: All external HTTP calls, database queries, and message queue operations must have explicit timeouts.
enforcement: AST scan: external call functions must include a timeout option
guardrails.reason: Without timeouts, a single slow external service can block all threads and crash the application.
verification: Verify all fetch, axios, and HTTP calls include a timeout parameter

guardrails.name: Security: CORS policy enforcement
guardrails.rule: CORS must be configured with an explicit allowlist of origins. Wildcard (*) origin is forbidden in production.
enforcement: Config scan: CORS configuration must not use wildcard origin
guardrails.reason: Wildcard CORS allows any website to make authenticated requests to the API, enabling CSRF and data theft.
verification: Verify CORS config uses an explicit origin allowlist and not *

guardrails.name: Security: File upload size limit
guardrails.rule: File upload endpoints must enforce a maximum file size (≤ 10MB by default) and validate file type against an allowlist.
enforcement: Pattern scan: file upload middleware must configure limits.fileSize and limits.allowedMimeTypes
guardrails.reason: Unlimited file uploads enable denial of service through disk exhaustion and potential malware upload.
verification: Verify upload middleware enforces size limits and validates file types against an allowlist

guardrails.name: Security: Input validation at boundary
guardrails.rule: All external inputs (request body, query params, path params, headers) must be validated using a schema validator (Zod, Joi, class-validator) before processing.
enforcement: Pattern scan: controller/route handlers must apply validation middleware or schema checks
guardrails.reason: Unvalidated input is the root cause of injection attacks, type confusion, and unexpected behavior.
verification: Verify each endpoint has a validation schema applied to its input parameters

guardrails.name: Security: Rate limiting configuration
guardrails.rule: All public API endpoints must have rate limiting applied.
enforcement: Architecture review: global rate limiter middleware or per-route rate limits must be configured
guardrails.reason: Without rate limiting, APIs are vulnerable to brute-force attacks, denial of service, and resource exhaustion.
verification: Verify rate limiting middleware is applied globally or per-route

guardrails.name: Security: XSS prevention (output encoding)
guardrails.rule: All user-provided data rendered in HTML must be escaped. Use template engines with auto-escaping or explicit encoding functions.
enforcement: Static scan: detect dangerouslySetInnerHTML, innerHTML assignment, and document.write usage
guardrails.reason: Unescaped user data in HTML enables cross-site scripting attacks that steal credentials and session tokens.
verification: Verify no user input is injected into DOM without encoding

guardrails.name: State: No direct global state mutation
guardrails.rule: Global state (Redux, Zustand, Pinia, etc.) must be modified through actions/mutations, not direct assignment.
enforcement: lint rule: no-direct-state-mutation
guardrails.reason: Direct state mutation bypasses change tracking, devtools, and time-travel debugging.
verification: Verify state changes go through actions/mutations

guardrails.name: TDD: Tests must exist before implementation
guardrails.rule: Every implementation file must have a corresponding test file. No production code without a test.
enforcement: CI: verify test files exist for all source files
guardrails.reason: Test-driven development requires tests to exist alongside or before production code. Code without tests is unverifiable.
verification: Verify each .ts/.js source file has a corresponding .test.ts/.test.js file

guardrails.name: Accessibility: Form inputs must have labels
guardrails.rule: All <input>, <select>, and <textarea> elements must be associated with a <label>.
enforcement: lint rule: jsx-a11y/label-has-associated-control
guardrails.reason: Unlabeled inputs are inaccessible to screen reader users.
verification: Verify all form inputs have associated labels

guardrails.name: Accessibility: Interactive elements must have accessible names
guardrails.rule: Buttons, links, and interactive elements must have aria-label, aria-labelledby, or visible text.
enforcement: lint rule: jsx-a11y/role-supports-aria-props
guardrails.reason: Screen readers cannot identify elements without accessible names, excluding users with disabilities.
verification: Verify all interactive elements have accessible names

guardrails.name: Accessibility: Sufficient color contrast
guardrails.rule: Text must have sufficient color contrast ratio (4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text).
enforcement: CSS lint rule for color contrast
guardrails.reason: Low contrast text is unreadable for users with visual impairments.
verification: Verify all text meets WCAG 2.1 AA contrast requirements

guardrails.name: API: Endpoints must be versioned
guardrails.rule: API endpoints must include version prefix (e.g., /api/v1/).
enforcement: CI: verify API routes have version prefix
guardrails.reason: Unversioned APIs break clients when the API changes, causing production incidents.
verification: Verify all API routes have version prefix

guardrails.name: CI/CD: Require PR approval before merge
guardrails.rule: Main branch must require at least one PR approval before merge.
enforcement: Repository settings: require PR reviews
guardrails.reason: Merging without review bypasses code quality checks and introduces unvetted changes.
verification: Verify branch protection rules require PR approval

guardrails.name: Data: Avoid SELECT * in queries
guardrails.rule: SQL queries must specify columns explicitly, not use SELECT *.
enforcement: Code review: specify columns explicitly
guardrails.reason: SELECT * retrieves unnecessary data, wastes bandwidth, and breaks when schema changes.
verification: Verify queries specify columns explicitly

guardrails.name: Data: Migrations must be versioned and reversible
guardrails.rule: Database migrations must have version numbers and up/down functions.
enforcement: CI: verify migration files are versioned
guardrails.reason: Unversioned migrations cause conflicts in team environments and cannot be rolled back.
verification: Verify migrations have version numbers and rollback support

guardrails.name: Infrastructure: Enable logging and monitoring
guardrails.rule: Cloud resources must have logging enabled (CloudWatch, Stackdriver, etc.).
enforcement: IaC scan: verify logging configuration
guardrails.reason: Without logging, security incidents and performance issues are invisible.
verification: Verify all cloud resources have logging enabled

guardrails.name: Mobile: No hardcoded API URLs
guardrails.rule: API base URLs must come from environment configuration, not hardcoded strings.
enforcement: Code review: use environment config for API URLs
guardrails.reason: Hardcoded URLs break when switching between dev/staging/production environments.
verification: Verify API URLs come from environment config

guardrails.name: Performance: Avoid heavy libraries in client bundle
guardrails.rule: Heavy libraries (moment.js, lodash full, pdf-lib) should use tree-shakable alternatives or dynamic imports.
enforcement: Code review: prefer date-fns, lodash-es, or dayjs
guardrails.reason: Large libraries inflate bundle size and slow initial page load.
verification: Verify bundle uses tree-shakable alternatives

guardrails.name: Performance: Connection pool configuration
guardrails.rule: Database connection pools must have min and max limits configured.
enforcement: Config scan: database configuration must specify pool size limits
guardrails.reason: Unbounded connection pools exhaust database connections under load and cause connection refused errors.
verification: Verify database config includes connection pool min and max settings

guardrails.name: Performance: Missing index warning
guardrails.rule: Fields used in WHERE clauses, JOIN conditions, or ORDER BY must be indexed.
enforcement: Schema review: fields referenced in queries must appear in database indexes
guardrails.reason: Missing indexes cause full table scans that degrade performance linearly with data growth.
verification: Cross-reference query WHERE/JOIN fields against schema index definitions

guardrails.name: Performance: N+1 query detection
guardrails.rule: Database queries must not be executed inside loops. Use batch queries, joins, or eager loading.
enforcement: AST scan: detect database query calls inside for/while/forEach/map loops
guardrails.reason: N+1 queries cause exponential performance degradation as data volume grows.
verification: Identify query calls inside loop bodies and verify they are replaced with batch operations

guardrails.name: Performance: Response size limits
guardrails.rule: API responses returning lists must implement pagination. Unbounded result sets are forbidden.
enforcement: Pattern scan: GET endpoints returning arrays must accept pagination parameters
guardrails.reason: Unbounded responses consume excessive memory and network bandwidth, and degrade client performance.
verification: Verify list-returning endpoints support limit/offset or cursor-based pagination

guardrails.name: Performance: Unbounded query warning
guardrails.rule: Database queries without LIMIT, pagination, or date range filters must be flagged for review.
enforcement: AST scan: findMany/findAll calls without take/limit/skip parameters
guardrails.reason: Queries without bounds return unbounded result sets that grow over time and cause memory exhaustion.
verification: Verify all data-fetching queries include limit, pagination, or date-range filters

guardrails.name: Security: Content Security Policy
guardrails.rule: HTML responses must include a Content-Security-Policy header or meta tag that disallows unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval.
enforcement: Header scan: CSP header must not include unsafe-inline or unsafe-eval directives
guardrails.reason: Unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval in CSP defeat XSS protections and allow script injection.
verification: Verify CSP header is set and does not contain unsafe-inline or unsafe-eval

guardrails.name: TDD: Minimum test coverage
guardrails.rule: New code must maintain minimum 80% line coverage. Coverage configuration must exist.
enforcement: CI: enforce coverage threshold in test runner config
guardrails.reason: Coverage thresholds ensure new code is actually tested, not just that test files exist.
verification: Verify test runner config exists with coverage threshold >= 80%

guardrails.name: TDD: No skipped or pending tests in production
guardrails.rule: Test files must not contain skipped (.skip), pending (.only), or disabled (xit/xdescribe) tests in committed code.
enforcement: CI: reject commits containing skipped tests
guardrails.reason: Skipped tests create false confidence. Every test must be active or explicitly removed, never hidden.
verification: Verify no .skip(), .only(), xit(), xdescribe(), or pending() calls exist in test files

guardrails.name: TDD: Tests must have assertions
guardrails.rule: Every test function must contain at least one assertion (expect/ assert/ should).
enforcement: CI: lint rule to verify assertions in test blocks
guardrails.reason: A test without assertions validates nothing. It runs code but never checks the result.
verification: Verify each test block contains at least one expect(), assert(), or should call

guardrails.name: Testing: Components must have render tests
guardrails.rule: Every UI component must have at least one render/snapshot test.
enforcement: CI: verify component test files exist
guardrails.reason: Render tests catch regression bugs in component output and prevent visual drift.
verification: Verify component test files exist for all UI components

guardrails.name: API: Consistent response envelope
guardrails.rule: API responses must use consistent envelope: { data, error, meta }.
enforcement: Code review: consistent response shape
guardrails.reason: Inconsistent response shapes make frontend integration error-prone and difficult to maintain.
verification: Verify API responses use consistent envelope format

guardrails.name: Errors: Structured error responses
guardrails.rule: Error responses must follow RFC 7807 Problem Details format or consistent structure.
enforcement: Code review: consistent error format
guardrails.reason: Structured errors enable automatic retry logic and consistent client-side error handling.
verification: Verify error responses follow consistent format
